name: Egba and Yoruba esusu savings clubs
description: Yoruba esusu groups pooled members’ contributions and distributed the collected sum in rotation, offering participants a way to accumulate capital.

impact.note: Rotating clubs gave people of one region a way to gather capital without banks, and diaspora and later savings clubs continued the practice.

date.basis: Shields dates Campbell’s observation to 1860; his cited account appeared later, in 1861.

events.statement: Campbell described Abeokuta mutual-saving societies formed chiefly by women, with weekly deposits distributed to one member at a time in rotation.
events.scope: Campbell’s report as cited by Shields; not the origin of esusu.

evidence.supports: Egba esusu clubs were described as chiefly formed by women.
Campbell describes women participants, weekly deposits, rotation and continued deposits after drawing.

contributions.resource: Formed and participated in mutual savings clubs.

evidence.supports: Shields reports Campbell’s observation about women’s participation.
The observer says the societies were chiefly formed by women.

date.label: Late 19th century
date.basis: Shields characterizes Johnson’s account as late nineteenth century; 1870–1900 is an approximate indexing interval, not a securely bounded period.

events.statement: A later Yoruba account describes regular contributions distributed to members in rotation.
events.scope: Regional practice reported in a later account, not necessarily the specific Egba groups observed in 1860.

evidence.supports: A later Yoruba account describes regular contributions distributed to members in rotation.

earliest_record.rationale: Date and scope follow the cited event; this is the earliest episode established in this research, not a claim of world priority.

caveats: Campbell describes the weekly rotation in the same passage as the women-led Abeokuta societies; he does not use the name esusu there. Shields connects his account with esusu; her later Yoruba account remains a separate witness. Campbell was an outside visitor and does not establish eligibility, the origin of the practice, or uniform rules across all groups.

research.note: Independent second reader checked the cited historical episodes, dates and actor roles against the stated source passages, subject to the caveats; other facets are not blanket reviewed. Wave 7 added sourced material; changed events await independent review. Independent review checked Campbell’s 1861 text: the same passage describes women and rotation. The later Johnson account and the specific 1860 observation date were not independently rechecked, so the overall events facet remains sourced.
